pages.text: "Dodo, I want to touch it too!" Little brother Mumu hopped under the willow. Big sister Dodo stood on her long legs and gently touched catkins at a branch tip. However high he jumped, his wingtip couldn't reach.
"Soft!" Dodo lifted her chin, touching the catkins. Mumu dropped to the ground. "Dodo has long legs and long wings... My legs are short," he murmured.
Mumu sat sadly on the mill doorstep. Tapping only his toes, he said, "Why are my legs so short?" His blue neck scarf drooped too.
Dad stopped on his way with a wheat sack. "Something worrying you?" Mumu sniffled. "Dad, my short legs can't reach the branch." Dad set down the sack and sat beside him.
Dad held Mumu's wing. "Do I have a neck, or not?" "No! Your head sits right on your body!" Mumu giggled. Dad laughed too. "Then Mumu..." he asked.

Wheat grains spilled through a gap in the sack. Pick, pick, pick! Mumu gathered them first. With short legs, the ground was close before him. Dad whispered, "Dodo for high branches, Mumu for the ground. So Mumu..."
Mumu's eyes grew bright. "Because Mumu is Mumu!" He proudly set his gathered grains on Dad's wing. A whole heap. Dodo ran from the willow. "Wow! You're really fast!"
Just then, one flick of Mumu's tail! His drooping blue scarf fluttered again. He hopped up and spread both wings wide.
Now the three worked together. Dad carried sacks, Dodo lifted them high onto the cart, and Mumu picked fallen grains. "Broad Dad, tall Dodo, quick Mumu!" All three laughed.
That evening, Dad patted Mumu's back with a wingtip. "The one and only Mumu in the world!" Short legs have things they do well too. Inside Dad's wing, Mumu called, "Because Mumu is Mumu!"
